question.problem: The $6$th and $7$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-37$ and $-43,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{6}=-37$ and ${a}_{7}=-43$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{7}-{a}_{6} \\  & =-43-(-37) \\  & =-43+37 \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{7}=-43,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{7}$ is $6$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{7} & ={a}_{1}+6d \\ -43 & ={a}_{1}+6(-6) \\ -43 & ={a}_{1}-36 \\ -43+36 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-7+(n-1)(-6) \\  & =-7-6n+6 \\  & =-6n-1.\end{aligned}
$$
